title: Saving for a goal
intro: A goal turns a price into a plan: what you've saved, what's left and how many weeks it takes.
explanation: Your goal counts what's in Save. Money that's due but not handed over yet doesn't count. Cash in Spend doesn't count either.
What's left is the price minus what's in Save. To find how many weeks, see how many times your weekly saving fits into what's left.
If it doesn't fit exactly, round up. The last bit still needs a whole week of saving.
Spending from Spend doesn't change your goal date, as long as you keep saving the same each week.

example.title: Working out the weeks
lines: 8 weeks gives {m:3200}, still short. 9 weeks gives {m:3600}.

practice.prompt: A goal costs {m:1400}. You start from zero and save {m:300} a week. How many weeks will it take?

misconceptions.feedback: Not quite. 4 weeks gives {m:1200}. That's {m:200} short, so round up to the next week.

practice.wrong: Not quite. See how many weeks of {m:300} it takes to reach {m:1400}.
hints: 4 weeks gives {m:1200}. Is that enough for {m:1400}?
practice.correct: That's it. 5 weeks. After 4 weeks you're {m:200} short, so you round up.
